{{Hatnote|Also named Agnès Sulem-Bialobroda, known as a violinist for the [[Rosamonde Quartet]]}}

'''Agnès Sulem''' (born 1959){{r|born}} is a French applied mathematician whose research topics include [[stochastic control]], [[jump diffusion]], and [[mathematical finance]].

== Education ==
Sulem earned a Ph.D. in 1983 at [[Paris Dauphine University]], with the dissertation '' Résolution explicite d'Inéquations Quasi-Variationnelles associées à des problèmes de gestion de stock'' supervised by [[Alain Bensoussan]].{{r|mg}}

== Career ==
She is a director of research at the [[French Institute for Research in Computer Science and Automation]] (INRIA) in Paris, where she heads the MATHRISK project on [[Financial risk modeling|mathematical risk handling]].{{r|inria}} She is currently a professor at the [[University of Luxembourg]] in the Mathematics department. She is a coauthor of the book ''Applied Stochastic Control of Jump Diffusions'' (with [[Bernt Øksendal]], Springer, 2005; 2nd ed., 2007; 3rd ed., 2019).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Agnès Sulem|url=https://www.rocq.inria.fr/mathfi/Sulem.html|access-date=2021-09-03|website=www.rocq.inria.fr}}</ref> Sulem is also an associate editor at the ''[[Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications]]'' and at the ''[[SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics]]''.
